_readme: HAND-LABELLED GROUND TRUTH FOR H-1B CLASSIFICATION.
Every record below was read individually and judged against one question:
should a professional monitoring H-1B receive this record? The judgement is
recorded with the reason, so it can be argued with rather than trusted.
The candidate pool was every record whose title or summary names H-1B (16),
plus every record the extractor classified as H-1B without such a mention
(5). That was 21 records judged on 2026-09-03, of which 19 are relevant and 2 are not.
On 2026-10-08 four records the classifier claimed after that date were judged
individually and added as relevant, each with its reason: 25 judged, 23 relevant.
The pool is deliberately NOT the set the classifier returns — scoring against
your own output is how a metric gets gamed. It is the set a reader could
identify from the archive text plus everything the classifier claimed.
Known limitation: a record that concerns H-1B without naming it anywhere in
its title, summary, or the extractor's evidence quote is invisible to this
pool and to us. The archive does not store document bodies, so that class
cannot be measured here and recall below is recall against what is knowable.

relevant.why: Executive Order 14431. Its title is about administering the H-1B nonimmigrant visa programme. Added 2026-10-08 (review welcome).

Proclamation restricting entry of certain nonimmigrant workers; its text sets the national-interest exception for employers hiring H-1B specialty-occupation workers, the same family as the September 2025 proclamation already labelled relevant. Added 2026-10-08 (review welcome).

Proposes removing the 60-day grace period after employment ends for nonimmigrant workers including H-1B holders; a laid-off H-1B worker's status depends on it. The extractor's quote is a statutory citation, but the rule's subject is squarely H-1B. Added 2026-10-08 (review welcome).
Correction to the Fee for Certain H-1B Petitions proposed rule (federal_register:2026-17324, already relevant). Title names it. Added 2026-10-08 (review welcome).
Proposes a fee on H-1B cap-subject petitions. Title names it.
DHS proposes an additional H-1B fee.
Fee applying to H-1B and L-1 visas.
FY2027 H-1B cap reached — operational fact an employer acts on.
FY2027 H-1B registration selection completed.
DOL wage-protection NPRM covering H-1B among other programmes.
FY2027 H-1B registration period opens.
Weighted selection for cap-subject H-1B petitions.
Changes the process for awarding H-1B visas.
Proclamation restricting entry, summary names H-1B petitions.
Weighted selection for cap-subject H-1B petitions (earlier stage).

USCIS guidance answering questions about the September 2025 proclamation restricting entry of certain nonimmigrant workers. It is titled H-1B FAQ and its summary is entirely about the H-1B program, so an employer monitoring H-1B needs it.
FY2026 H-1B cap reached.
FY2026 H-1B selection completed.
FY2026 H-1B registration period opens.
H-1B final rule and revised Form I-129 effective date.
Mandatory e-filing. The evidence quote is specifically about H-1B cap registration having to be filed electronically, which is an operational change for every H-1B filer.
relevant.note: Body-only evidence, but the quote is about H-1B itself rather than a citation.

relevant.why: Premium processing fee increase. Premium processing is requested on Form I-907 against Form I-129, which is the H-1B petition, so H-1B filers pay this.
relevant.note: Weakest of the relevant set: the quoted evidence names H-2B and R-1 rather than H-1B. Correct match, poor quote.

relevant.why: Proclamation restricting entry of certain nonimmigrant workers; evidence quotes a direction about beneficiaries of approved H-1B petitions.

notRelevant.why: An H-2A adverse-effect wage rate rule. It was classified H-1B because its body says the statutory provision 'was enacted in the context of the H-1B ... classification'. That is a historical aside about section 212(p), not this rule's scope.
A rule about signatures on benefit requests generally. It was classified H-1B from a footnote citing a 2011 H-1B registration NPRM (76 FR 11686).
